subject.title: [Bug]: GitHub Copilot anthropic-messages transport silently hangs ~365s in isolated cron sessions (2026.5.27)

question: After live current-main GitHub Copilot Claude cron proof, should aborted/no-output Copilot runs enter model fallback, or should OpenClaw rely on the 60-second idle-timeout path plus cron error status?
rationale: The remaining behavior is not purely mechanical because fallback after an abort can recover delivery but may also repeat tools or external writes after partial execution.

options.title: Prove first, fallback narrowly
options.body: Run live current-main Copilot cron proof, then allow fallback only for idle-timeout failures before tool or outbound side effects are observed.

options.title: Fallback on aborted no-output
options.body: Treat aborted/no-output Copilot results as fallback-worthy even when the original stream ended without a terminal response.

options.title: Keep current policy
options.body: Keep current cron error surfacing and stream-stall handling without adding a new aborted-result retry path.

recommendation.title: Prove first, fallback narrowly
recommendation.body: Run live current-main Copilot cron proof, then allow fallback only for idle-timeout failures before tool or outbound side effects are observed.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current history on Copilot Claude routing and provider stream seams where the remaining fallback policy would likely land.
